title: Patatas a la Riojana
description: The traditional build: water rather than stock, no tomato, and the potatoes fried in the rendered chorizo fat before any liquid goes in.

items.note: Or 300ml stock topped up with water

steps.text: Tear the potatoes ({{potatoes}}) rather than cutting them. Push the knife in about 1.5cm, then twist and break the piece off. The ragged starchy faces are what thicken the broth.
Shallots ({{shallots}}), garlic ({{garlic}} cloves) and capsicum ({{capsicum}}) into the bowl. Chop 4 sec / Speed 5. Scrape down.
Add the olive oil ({{oil}}). Sauté 5 min / 120°C / Reverse / Soft stir until soft, without colouring.
Add the chorizo ({{chorizo}}). Cook 3 min / 120°C / Reverse / Soft stir until the fat runs orange.
Add the potatoes and cook 10 min / 120°C / Reverse / Soft stir so they coat in the fat and start to catch. Most of the flavour comes from this step.
Add the wine ({{wine}}) and reduce 3 min / Varoma / Reverse / Soft stir, MC off.

Add the paprika (1 tsp sweet plus a pinch of hot), bay leaves ({{bay}}) and water ({{water}}). Cook 30 min / 100°C / Reverse / Soft stir, MC off with the basket on the lid, until the potatoes give to a knife but hold their shape.
Rest 10 minutes uncovered so the broth thickens. Taste for salt last.

notes.title: Water, not stock
notes.text: The traditional approach. The chorizo does the seasoning, and 250g of it plus a salty stock would be aggressive.

notes.title: Capacity
notes.text: This lands close to 2.0L. If it looks high at step 7, hold back 100ml of the water and add it midway.

notes.title: Thickening
notes.text: If it stays thin, mash 2–3 potato pieces back through. Cornflour slurry is texturally wrong for this style.

notes.title: Tomato variation
notes.text: Tomato is not part of the classic. To use fresh ones up, deseed, salt and drain them 15 minutes, then add two chopped at step 7. That is the July version of this recipe, which also used tomato paste and 300ml stock.

notes.title: Speed setting
notes.text: Reverse / Soft stir from step 3 onward. Speed 1 is only justified for short early steps to stop catching.

notes.title: Choricero
notes.text: Choricero pepper paste is the authentic regional ingredient. Hard to find here, so smoked paprika plus green capsicum is the reasonable substitute.
